title: Grateful Dead Live at Dream Bowl on 1969-02-21
lineage: SBD > MR > ? > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a raging ’69 with a monster Eleven, Dark Star and St. Stephen.
ai_review.review: The recording is a high‑fidelity soundboard tape that most reviewers describe as crisp and “crystal clear,” despite occasional faint high‑frequency hiss. Musically the show is hailed as one of the band’s fiercest ’69 performances – the Eleven, Dark Star, St. Stephen, Morning Dew and Lovelight receive glowing praise, with only the chaotic ending of Doin’ That Rag noted as a minor blemish. Overall it’s a must‑have for anyone collecting the peak 1969 Dead.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews (≈85%) are enthusiastic, awarding 4–5 stars and highlighting superb playing and excellent soundboard quality; only a few off‑topic low‑star posts drag the average down, so the combined show‑and‑recording rating is strong.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers repeatedly call the tape "crystal clear" and "awesome sound quality for ’69," with only a brief mention of a faint high‑frequency hiss that does not detract from overall clarity.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A shorter-than‑usual set that never loses momentum – the first half builds solidly and the second half erupts with fire, delivering a tightly woven flow of high‑energy jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as "raging" and "surpassing the limits of the mind," his guitar work is repeatedly praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for an on‑stage outburst at the end of Doin' That Rag, calling someone a "motherfucker"; reviewers also query what sparked the incident.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey's screaming and cussing during the chaotic ending of Doin' That Rag is mentioned as a rough spot.
